questions.explanation: The common difference is $-3$, so the $n$th term starts with $-3n$. When $n = 1$: $-3(1) = -3$, but the first term is $10$, so we add $13$. The $n$th term is $-3n + 13$.

questions.stem: Is $100$ a term in the sequence with $n$th term $7n + 2$?

options.text: No, because $n$ would not be a whole number

questions.explanation: Set $7n + 2 = 100$. Then $7n = 98$, so $n = 14$. Since $14$ is a whole number, $100$ is the $14$th term of the sequence.

questions.stem: Is $50$ a term in the sequence with $n$th term $4n + 1$?

options.text: No, because $n$ would not be a whole number

questions.explanation: Set $4n + 1 = 50$. Then $4n = 49$, so $n = 12.25$. Since this is not a whole number, $50$ is not a term in the sequence.
